reason: Narrower: the green photosynthetic cells of a Sphagnum leaf that alternate with the hyaline cells ('exposed on both surfaces', 'trapezoidal in cross section'). PO_0000076 is a parenchyma cell with chloroplasts. Use the moss leaf, non-vascular leaf PO_0025075, as the whole.
A generic part ('wing' was rejected on 2026-11-13) that needs the organ it belongs to. It could be a wing of a fruit, a mericarp rib, a seed or a calyx. 'Dorsal' gives a position, not the organ.
Exact: PO lists 'leaf lamina apex' as a synonym of leaf apex (as in rule C268, leaf blade apex). When the lamina is a leaflet's, use leaflet apex FLOPO_0986000.

Narrower: in Cyperaceae each spikelet scale subtends one flower. PO glume PO_0009039 is defined as one of a pair subtending the florets (the grass glume), so it does not fit. A scale that bears a flower is a flower bract.

target: inflorescence (PO_0009049): the region of an androgynous spike that bears pistillate flowers (PO_0025599)
reason: In Carex, the pistillate portion of a spike that bears both male and female flowers. Express it as a region of the spike (inflorescence part of a qualified whole: has part some pistillate flower). A perigynium count is a count of parts of this region.
A shape quality (acicular) of the spines or hairs that follow it ('needlelike spines on costa'). The bearer is the noun after it.
A rate of flowering ('flowers 1 opening per day'). The bearer is the flower and the statement is about timing, not a structure.
Narrower: the nectar glands on cactus areoles, such as Ferocactus, are extrafloral nectaries ('seasonally conspicuous', 'dome-shaped').
The second term of a ratio ('2--3 x as long as perianth'). Use pattern 10 (equality and ratio to another part), with perianth PO_0009058 as the other part.
Narrower: culm is a PO synonym of stem PO_0009047, so a culm internode is a stem internode of a grass or sedge.

target: leaf apex (PO_0020137): the cusp is its abrupt terminal point
reason: A cusp is the sharp point at the leaf apex. 'Toothed' and 'long' describe the apex region. A separate 'cusp' class would duplicate the mucro/acumen cases that were rejected as generic.

target: costa (PO_0030072): its cells on the adaxial surface; '4 cells wide' is a count of parts (pattern 03) across the costa at mid-leaf
reason: Moss leaf costa. The statements count the costal cells across the adaxial side, or describe their shape (quadrate). Use costa as the whole, with the adaxial surface as the region.

Narrower: French nucule = nutlet, one of the four one-seeded parts of the fruit of Boraginaceae and Lamiaceae ('formés de 4 nucules', 'cohérentes par paires'). PO mericarp is a carpellate unit of a schizocarp. The botanical_terminology mapping of nutlet to fruit is too broad.

label: floral spur
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009046 flower
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a flower (PO:0009046) that is a hollow, tubular or sac-like extension of a petal, sepal, labellum or corolla, often containing nectar.
reason: A real structure in many floras (Orchidaceae, Aquilegia, Viola, Balsaminaceae, Linaria). It has no PO class: PO 'spur' is a synonym of short shoot PO_0004701, so 'spur' is grounded wrongly today. Should be proposed to PO upstream.

label: velum
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009026 sporophyll
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a thin membranous fold of the adaxial base of a sporophyll (PO:0009026) partly or wholly covering the sporangium (PO:0025094), as in Isoetes.
reason: A standard diagnostic character in Isoetes ('velum complete', 'velum absent'). 'Shiny black and reticulate' is probably a misparse of the next statement (the spores). Keep it FLOPO-local first; it can be proposed to PO with the fern and lycophyte terms (indusium).
Narrower: small clusters of stone cells (sclerids, PO_0025418) in the flesh of a fruit, i.e. portions of sclerenchyma that are part of the fruit (PO_0009001). Same target as 'sclerotic granule'.
'Segment' was rejected as a generic part, so its margin is generic too. It could be the margin of a perianth segment, a leaf segment or a frond segment.

A count of branches per node: the part is a branch, and 'per node' only says where they are counted ('per node' was rejected on 2026-11-13). Use pattern 03 (count of parts) with stem node PO_0020141, or inflorescence axis for a rachis.

label: tegula
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of FLOPO_0986017 rostellum
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a stalk of an orchid pollinarium derived from the epidermis of the rostellum (FLOPO:0986017), connecting the pollinia (FLOPO:0986016) to the viscidium (FLOPO:0986032).
reason: An orchid pollinarium part with no class. Siblings viscidium and caudicle are already FLOPO-local. Do not map 'tegula stipe' to the PO stalk rule (stipe -> stalk), which is about fern, gynoecium and fruit stipes. Propose to PO with the orchid batch.
Narrower: a small lobe of an orchid lip (size 0.2-0.3 mm, fimbriate or erose margin). If the source is a two-lipped corolla, use corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006 instead.
Narrower: a branchlet is an ultimate branch of the inflorescence. PO lists 'inflorescence branch' as a synonym of PO_0009081.

Narrower: the cells of the moss stem's central strand ('small', 'poorly or not differentiated'). These qualities describe the strand. The cells themselves are hydroids (PO_0025032) when that distinction matters.

target: papilla cell (PO_0025166) as part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075)
reason: Papillae on the cells of a moss leaf lamina. 'Papilla' already maps to papilla cell (C269). 'Laminal' gives the whole: the moss leaf, i.e. non-vascular leaf (pattern 12, part of a qualified whole).

label: anther wing
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009066 anther
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a stiff, membranous lateral flange of an anther (PO:0009066); adjacent wings form the guide rails that lead the pollinator to the corpusculum, as in Asclepiadoideae.
reason: A standard character in Apocynaceae-Asclepiadoideae (shape 'right-triangular', 'closed', length). The generic 'wing' cannot carry it. Propose to PO with the gynostegium (PO issue 6).
A colour mark ('red dots basally'): a spotted colour pattern of the petal or tepal, not a structure. The bearer is the organ the dots are on.
Narrower: same as 'sclerotic granules'. A cluster of sclerids in the fruit flesh, counted 'per fruit' (part of fruit PO_0009001).

A misspelling of areola or areole. In these examples it reads as seed-coat reticulum cells ('ca. 50 longitudinal rows', 'end walls raised'), but the organ is not given. 'Areole' was rejected as generic.

Ambiguous: it could be the bracts of a fruiting catkin ('those at middle of cones', as in Betulaceae: inflorescence bract), cone scales (megasporophyll PO_0009027), or scales on a fruit surface ('bristly', 'fringed'). These need different targets.

label: bract scar
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0025029 shoot axis
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the mark left on a shoot axis (PO:0025029), such as a peduncle, where a bract (PO:0009055) has been shed.
reason: A sibling of leaf scar FLOPO_0986052, which applies to leaves, not bracts. It is used only in counts ('with 2 bract scars'). Better: propose to PO a common parent 'phyllome scar' with leaf scar under it.
Narrower: sheathing, bract-like scale leaves on a scape or peduncle, counted ('with 2-4 bract-like sheaths'). If they subtend flowers, use bract PO_0009055 instead.
